transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 63 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, Catalyst), Tom Becker (Infra Eng, Catalyst), Priya Shah (CTO, Catalyst)

Summary:
Redwood Optimize console walkthrough focused on batching + prefix/KV prefetch recommendations and a cost model tailored to Catalyst Distributors' conversational product. Marcus demonstrated console scenarios and cost simulation; discussion covered latency vs unit cost tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted, data residency and KMS concerns. Agreed next steps to exchange cost spreadsheet and sample traffic.

Topics:
- Prefetch (look-ahead) vs session KV cache
- Batching window sizing and concurrency policies
- Cost model scenarios (tokens, GPU-hours, reserved capacity)
- Security: KMS, VPC, audit logs
- Pilot runway and acceptance criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (AE): hey everyone thanks for carving time. um quick intros? we can go around.
[00:10] Lena: sure lena here, we run recommendations and chat flows for our distributor network. i'm head of ml.
[00:15] Tom: tom infra, we own deployment and security.
[00:18] Priya: priya, cto, i'll mostly listen for infra impacts and sso needs.
[00:22] Sofia: great. marcus is our se, he'll walk through Optimize in console and run a quick prefetch/caching cost sim.
[00:30] Marcus (SE): hi all, thanks. quick agenda: show console playbook, cost model, then Q&A and we sketch a pilot.

[02:05] Marcus: first slide — apologies, bit of a screen lag — but here's the Optimize module, the prefetch panel, we call it "lookahead prefetch" in the UI, sometimes the logs show it as prefetch or look-ahead. it lets you select prefix depth and TTL.
[02:45] Tom: wait, quick question — is this the kv cache you're talking about? our infra folks call it distributed kv, is it sticky to a session?
[02:52] Marcus: yes. two modes: session KV (session affinity, stored in local GPU KV cache for 10-60 mins depending) and global prefetch (we precompute KV for hot prefixes and keep them in a distributed cache with TTL). session is lower latency but needs session affinity; prefetch helps cold starts.
[03:30] Lena: how do you decide which prefixes to prefetch at what size? our catalog has long product descriptions so prefixes vary.
[03:39] Marcus: good question. console recommends by frequency + token-cost delta; we run an analysis over your historical prompts and simulate lookahead cost vs saved generation tokens. the rule-of-thumb we showed — if a prefix appears > X% of queries and saves > Y tokens per hit, prefetch pays off. i'll show the sim.

[06:10] Marcus: switching to the cost model tab — this is the tailored sheet. entering a few numbers for the demo: monthly requests 2.2M, average prompt length 90 tokens, average generation 280 tokens, peak concurrent qps 600 with bursts to 2k.
[06:35] Sofia: we pulled these from the brief you sent, lena — thanks.

[07:10] Marcus: baseline hosted inference at current model v yields $Z per token, with no prefetching, your unit cost sits at ~$0.0007 per output token. with prefetch for the top 12 prefixes (covering ~18% of volume) you can reduce net token generation by ~22% in the sim. but prefetch adds memory + occasional extra compute to populate caches.
[07:55] Tom: memory on the GPU? or external cache?
[08:00] Marcus: both options — on-GPU session KV is fastest but uses GPU memory; distributed prefetch uses an external Redis-like store (we support both managed options or your self-hosted endpoint in VPC). memory costs vs token-savings trade.

[09:40] Marcus: here's a modeled scenario — 3 prefetch tiers: shallow (prefix 8 tokens), mid (16 tokens), deep (32 tokens). shallow gives quick wins for short greetings and boilerplate; deep helps when full product context is required. deep prefetch can save up to 45% of tokens for long prompts in our sample sets but has higher cache fill cost.

[12:20] Priya: how does this interact with batching? if we batch aggressively we're already amortizing kernel overhead, does prefetch still help?
[12:30] Marcus: yes. batching reduces per-request compute but prefetch reduces the number of decode tokens you need to run. they multiply: batching reduces per-token latency overhead, prefetch reduces token count. console sim shows combined effect is non-linear — best results when batch size is optimized for your latency SLO and prefetch covers high-frequency prefixes.

[15:05] Marcus: demo: i enable mid prefetch for top 15 prefixes. console shows expected hit rate 0.19, predicted net token reduction 21%, and projected monthly savings $12k. switching to session-affinity mode increases hit rate to 0.26 but requires sticky routing.
[15:42] Tom: sticky routing = session affinity on the runtime? what's impact on autoscale?
[15:48] Marcus: slight; affinity pins a user to a shard while active, which can reduce scheduling flexibility. autoscaling still works but you may need higher overhead headroom to maintain SLOs during spikes. we include that in the cost sim.

[18:00] Lena: any differences if we run Redwood Dedicated vs hosted API?
[18:08] Marcus: dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lets you tune memory profiles and prefetch eviction policies more aggressively. hosted is simpler to start and can do prefetch via managed cache; Dedicated reduces unit GPU cost at high sustained volume. console cost comparison tab shows break-even at ~3.1M monthly requests for your current profile.

[21:30] Marcus: next, TTL and eviction strategies — we recommend adaptive TTLs: higher for evergreen prefixes (e.g., greetings) and short for product IDs that change. the console can auto-suggest TTL based on prefix volatility.

[23:40] Marcus: small demo glitch — the prefetch sim used a replaced token rate from a prior demo, so numbers update when i upload your csv. but pattern holds: top 10% prefixes often account for ~40% of hits in commerce chat.

[26:10] Tom: we worry about PII and retention — if we prefetch user-specific data, how is that encrypted?
[26:18] Marcus: good, security first. prefetch can be configured to not cache PII or to encrypt at rest using your KMS. in Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) your KMS manages keys; we also provide audit logs for every cache fill/eviction. SOC 2 artifacts and our security pack will be shared.

[29:05] Priya: what about failover? if cache is stale or misses, is there graceful fallback?
[29:12] Marcus: console supports automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. you can set ordered fallbacks: local KV -> distributed prefetch -> cold generation. we also support probabilistic prefetch warming to avoid cold-thundering herd.

[32:00] Marcus: i'm going to toggle a scenario for concurrency. here's 2k burst sim with and without prefetch, batching 8 vs 24. without prefetch, 95th latency jumps to 480ms; with mid prefetch + batching 16, 95th drops to 220ms and cost per request goes down 18%.

[35:10] Lena: those latency numbers assume network RTT of X? our customers in EMEA see higher RTT.
[35:17] Marcus: right, we let you set region RTTs in the sim. moving to eu-west region raises 95th by ~40ms in the model; that's why smart routing is useful — pin EU traffic to eu nodes and prefetch those prefixes in-region.

[38:45] Tom: curious on tooling: how do we monitor cache hit/miss and per-route cost?
[38:51] Marcus: Console has per-prefix hit rate heatmaps, token-saved metrics, and cost attribution down to route/token level. you can export CSVs and connect to our tracing hooks for deeper analysis.

[41:30] Marcus: small demo of the Optimize Alerts — set regressions on token-savings per prefix. if hit rate drops or model change increases token output, you get an alert tied to the eval suite.

[44:55] Priya: on contract/SLAs: if we go dedicated, what uptime and latency SLAs exist?
[45:02] Sofia: dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll share the SLA doc. enterprise support adds faster incident response.

[47:20] Tom: one more nit: how invasive is the pilot? can we run prefetch-only in front of current model without changing inference infra?
[47:28] Marcus: yes. we can run prefetch as a sidecar or managed cache that feeds into your existing endpoints — minimal change. for deeper savings we'd eventually move to session affinity + optimized batching in our runtime.

[50:10] Marcus: i'm going to sketch the recommended pilot: 4-week pilot, goals: validate 20% token reduction on top prefixes, keep 95th latency within 20% of baseline, and no PII cached. steps: 1) share traffic histogram, 2) Redwood config prefetch for top N prefixes, 3) run A/B for 2 weeks, 4) evaluate cost metrics.

[52:05] Lena: sounds reasonable. expected engineering time?
[52:10] Marcus: initial setup ~3-5 engineering days to map routes and wire the cache; A/B instrumentation another 2 days. could be faster if we use hosted managed cache.

[54:40] Sofia: quick pricing note — we will send a few scenarios: hosted on-demand, reserved dedicated monthly commit, and hybrid. each has prefetch + memory cost lines.

[56:22] Tom: any limitations on model types? we use a custom finetuned Llama variant.
[56:30] Marcus: we support major open architectures and finetuned variants; kernel selection and quantization are tuned per-model in our runtime. some very large seq-lengths may shift the sweet spot for prefetch depth. we'll validate during pilot.

[59:05] Priya: ok last Q — compliance: can you give us SOC2 + ISO pack and example audit logs for cache fills?
[59:14] Sofia: yes we'll include security pack and sample audit logs. also can show RBAC and SSO setup.

[61:00] Sofia: recap: Marcus will run throughput sketch for 2k burst and share that; i'll send cost-model spreadsheet and pricing scenarios; Catalyst (lena) will share traffic histogram and SLOs. pump through dates?
[61:20] Lena: we'll aim to send traffic by monday 2027-01-11.
[61:25] Marcus: i'll get the sim out by friday 2027-01-08.
[61:30] Sofia: i'll send cost scenarios by 2027-01-06.
[62:00] Priya: thanks everyone, that was useful.
[62:10] Meeting end.
